text:
Ravi Menon: Heads-up: the Optimize page shows a tooltip for 'Batching mode: Aggressive' that scrolls long and feels technical. Screenshot: https://redwood/mockups/optimize-batching.png

Nora Blake: I noticed that too. Current tooltip is: "Aggressive batching combines requests to maximize GPU utilization. May increase tail latency for interactive requests. Recommended for high-throughput workloads." Kinda dense.

Ivy Park: Agree. We need something shorter and actionable. Also this tooltip appears on hover and keyboard focus; make sure it's readable by screen readers (aria-describedby) and not truncated in translations.

Theo Vargas: Proposal A (short): "Aggressive batching: lower cost, higher throughput. Not ideal for latency-sensitive requests."

Nora Blake: Proposal B (even shorter): "Aggressive batching — cheaper but may add latency."

Ivy Park: I like B for concise UI, but we should link to docs for details: a small inline "Learn more" link that opens /docs/optimize#batching. Tooltip must include link text for keyboard users.

Ravi Menon: UX note: tooltips should be single sentence where possible. Avoid punctuation that breaks localization tools. Also ensure the tooltip arrow doesn't overlap long copy on narrow screens.

Theo Vargas: Accessibility checklist:
- Tooltip is reachable via keyboard (focus on the badge)
- `role=tooltip` + `aria-describedby` on the badge target
- Tooltip is dismissible with Esc
- Link inside tooltip must be focusable and announced as link text
- Tooltip should not rely on hover-only to convey critical info

Nora Blake: For tone, prefer familiar language: "cheaper" vs "lower cost"? Which is better for our docs style guide?

Ivy Park: Docs style prefers "lower cost" for professionalism, but UI can use friendlier "cheaper". Maybe: "Cheaper, higher throughput; may increase latency." in the tooltip, and the docs keep formal phrasing.

Ravi Menon: Example final copy for tooltip: "Cheaper, higher throughput — may increase latency. Learn more." Keeps it short, has link.

Theo Vargas: Also include a11y hint in tooltip DOM: `data-a11y-note="Batching can affect latency; see docs"` so automated checks catch it.

DesignBot: Created ticket: design/optimize - batching tooltip short copy + a11y. Reference: /docs/a11y/tooltips.

Nora Blake: I'll update Figma and push a tiny PR with the copy + the Learn more link and the accessibility attributes.

Ivy Park: I'll review the PR for screen reader text and localization char limits.

Ravi Menon: Thanks all :thumbsup:
